items.title: Certain Carbon and Alloy Steel Cut-to-Length Plate From the Republic of Korea: Notice of Court Decision Not in Harmony With the Results of Countervailing Duty Administrative Review; Notice of Amended Final Results

evidence.text: On October 27, 2026, the U.S. Court of International Trade (CIT) issued its final judgment in POSCO v. United States Consol. Court No. 24-00006, Slip Op. 26-131, sustaining the U.S. Department of Commerce (Commerce)'s second remand results pertaining to the administrative review of the countervailing duty (CVD) order on of certain carbon and alloy steel cut-to-length plate (CTL Plate) from the Republic of Korea (Korea) covering the period January

On December 13, 2023, Commerce published its Final Results in the 2021 CVD administrative review of CTL Plate from Korea. [ 1 ] In the Final Results, Commerce found that POSCO, the sole mandatory respondent, received countervailable subsidies from the Government of Korea (GOK) during the period of review (POR). Commerce calculated an overall net subsidy rate of 0.87 percent ad valorem. [ 2 ]

POSCO appealed Commerce's Final Results. On August 8, 2025, the CIT remanded the Final Results to Commerce, directing Commerce to reconsider the following: (1) Commerce's finding that the provision of electricity for less than adequate renumeration (LTAR) in Korea was de facto specific under section 771(5A)(D)(iii)(III) of the Tariff Act of 1930, as amended (the Act); (2) Commerce's finding that the provision of Korean Emission Trading System (K-

In the Second Final Remand Redetermination, [ 7 ] issued on July 11, ( printed page 70053) 2026, Commerce determined that the provision of K-ETS permits is de facto specific, pursuant to section 771(5A)(D)(iii)(I) of the Act. Based on this analysis, Commerce calculated a revised 0.80 percent total ad valorem subsidy rate for POSCO. On October 27, 2026, the CIT sustained Commerce's Second Final Remand Redetermination. items.title: Circular Welded Non-Alloy Steel Pipe From the Republic of Korea: Final Results of Antidumping Duty Administrative Review; 2023-2024

evidence.text: The U.S. Department of Commerce (Commerce) determines that Hyundai Steel Company (Hyundai Steel) and Hyundai Steel Pipe Co., Ltd. (HSP) made sales of subject merchandise at less than normal value (NV) during the period of review (POR), November 1, 2023, through October 31, 2024. Commerce determines that Husteel Co., Ltd. (Husteel) did not make sales of subject merchandise at less than NV during the POR.

On May 13, 2026, Commerce published the Preliminary Results in the Federal Register and invited interested parties to comment. [ 1 ] On August 25, 2026, Commerce extended the deadline for the final results of this review by 53 days. [ 2 ] The deadline for these final results is November 2, 2026. On August 26, 2026, we received timely-filed case briefs from Hyundai Steel/HSP. [ 3 ] On September 1, 2026, Wheatland Tube, a domestic interested party,

As provided in section 782(i) of the Act, in May, June, and August 2026, Commerce conducted on-site verifications of the sales and cost data reported by Husteel and Hyundai Steel/HSP. We used standard verification procedures, including an examination of relevant accounting and sales records, and original source documentation provided by Husteel [ 8 ] and Hyundai Steel/HSP. [ 9 ]

Based on our review of the record and our analysis of the comments received, Commerce made certain changes to the weighted-average dumping margin calculations for Husteel and Hyundai Steel/HSP. For further discussion of these changes, see the Issues and Decision Memorandum.
